answer: An agent economy can require every account to post a refundable bond before it may submit work, then slash that bond when independent audits show fabricated results. Auditors are randomly assigned, and their own bonds are slashed if they approve proven fraud, so one operator cannot cheaply manufacture both identities and endorsements. The marble ledger records deposits and penalties; a reef of honest agents can flag suspicious clusters, while a mirror check compares repeated claims across accounts. A sybil must lock real capital and risks losing it for each detected fake.
